Algieba.0820cdfb.text: Above you, three courtiers flicker and go out. Not one of the others will meet your eyes.

Algieba.0a15918d.text: When you go, he is sitting by the bed, holding her hand. Maren Sorrel has lost her scholar, and Ivo Rime has nothing left to try.

Algieba.0f3bbece.text: Old pages crumble under hurried hands, and an hour goes to dust. Then Lark lifts down a ledger in a careful, tired hand.

Algieba.100ea475.text: Halden's hand lies flat on a ledger he has not opened. He knows the numbers without looking. He has known them a long time.

Algieba.10a4dd9f.text: The Vale cannot live without the flame. Therefore the Vale must not know its price. So ordered, and so sealed.

Algieba.1260ea0f.text: Afterwards, you cannot say what it was. Only that there is a quiet place now, where something used to sing.

Algieba.12a7c39a.text: You wrap the lantern in oilcloth and carry it the way you carried cargo past the Ash Market's lanterns. No one on the road ever knows what passed them.

Algieba.12f0e9a5.text: For a breath Vorga doesn't answer. Behind him, the Host's warriors glance at one another.

Algieba.146270fd.text: A perfect stroke. The kind they tell about later.

Algieba.147ca25c.text: The canyon road ends at a bridge of rope and old timber. On the far side stands a wall of shields painted with suns.

Algieba.14b67491.text: And the ground takes one more.

Algieba.15abd1fa.text: Children who were silent a week ago chase each other round the tents, shrieking. Mother Skarrow pretends not to notice.

Algieba.15b125d7.text: A knot of young goblins holds the middle span, faces painted red, spears levelled. Their war cry is a name. Vorga.

Algieba.15c87f57.text: Bree sits down across from you. She doesn't sit down often. From her apron she takes a small book, soft with handling.

Algieba.16e370eb.text: She stops. The humming stops with her. The fire pops, very loud.

Algieba.17ed1a88.text: The boy opens his eyes. The last part, he says, is not the song.

Algieba.19dc4116.text: The first true winter in four hundred years comes down on the Vale. The warm fields freeze. The ford stops steaming.

Algieba.1a79af9c.text: When you leave, the dead are waiting at the gate of the hold, all facing the caves above the pass. Something up there is pulling at them.

Algieba.1b5afeef.text: The fire in the lantern leans towards the mountains, and so, you realise, do you. You have always been walking this way.

Algieba.1d583ac4.text: If you are reading this, Corvin, you have forgotten again. Stop reading by the ember-lamp. It takes something every time.

Algieba.1d59d5db.text: She is right. On the third shelf from the floor lies a roll of plans, bound in iron and stamped with the Warden seal.

Algieba.1e9e8e00.text: The town council meets in the back room of the Last Coal. It is warmer in here than the council deserves.

Algieba.1ea05553.text: The waystation is quiet. Among the Kindled packs lies a journal, its pages swollen with marsh water.

Algieba.1ec7e656.text: A smith forgets his trade. A mother forgets her son's face. A whole village forgets the road it came by.

Algieba.1f143ec1.text: Ahead, figures climb the road through the snow: pilgrims in Warden grey, a dwarf with a mason's hammer, a goliath carrying nothing.

Algieba.1f1bd0e9.text: You make camp in the lee of a frozen shrine below the pass. The fire is small, and it is wood. Nobody reaches for ember-light any more.

Algieba.234b3798.text: Up in Ember Keep, a dead Keeper tends a living fire, and writes down everything the Vale forgets.

Algieba.2353d08e.text: I came to seal this in with the rest, but the door was shut for good. Let whoever opens it know.

Algieba.25a0225b.text: The last of the hotheads flee east along the road, toward the far hills, and Vorga, wherever he is.

Algieba.27b158f7.text: The fighting is over. On the old stones of the bridge, Mother Skarrow lies where she fell.

Algieba.284a466c.text: Half a day past the canyon, the sand gives way to a stair cut into old stone. At the bottom, a door marked with the Wardens' flame.

Algieba.28ff04f6.text: It matches. Maud never touched the fire either. Two people in the Vale who truly remember that night, and they agree.

Algieba.297f74f2.text: The embers burn together in the Hall of the Flame. The heat of them is like a summer you only half remember.

Algieba.29dd98d0.text: Something in them settles, sure and new.

Algieba.2a4cecd9.text: Stars over the Greywall, the same as they ever were. Or nearly.

Algieba.2a4d99b8.text: Emberwick, at the Ashen Ford. The ground is warm underfoot, and the river steams in the evening cold.

Algieba.2a613889.text: It reads: We have learned what the fire takes. Each time it is used, it burns a memory away, and it does not give it back.

Algieba.2aab53bf.text: The notes are a doctor's case files. Nell's pulse, Nell's colour, how far Nell walked each day she walked. Eleven years of a single patient.

Algieba.2bbf198d.text: A little stronger now. A little harder to break.

Algieba.2c0b9829.text: Noon in the Sunscar. The sand has turned to glass in places, and the light comes up off it as hard as it comes down.

Algieba.2eb59af3.text: You set his account against Maud's, line by line. The red sky. The ember coming down like a thrown stone. A hooded figure on the hill.

Algieba.2f5fb512.text: The others wait at the edge of the firelight while she whispers it into your shoulder. Then she lets you bring them close.

Algieba.300d8734.text: In her cupped hands she carries the Mirewood ember. Already the edges of her are thinning, like mist in the morning.

Algieba.305ccff9.text: Night comes down cold and fast. Under the Tent of Cool Water, for the first time in weeks, the party sleeps without a watch.

Algieba.3118f5c6.text: For a heartbeat, the whole field goes still.

Algieba.3157bab4.text: The Hooded Stranger steps out from between the shelves, as if they had always been there. Perhaps they had.

Algieba.32e9cc01.text: The pool shows you a country on fire under a strange sky, and a great hall built around an empty space where a fire used to be.

Algieba.33c67e9b.text: Over flatbread and bitter tea, the elder tells the party what the desert knows, and Lark puts it into the valley tongue.

Algieba.3466a555.text: She lifts her hand. The first of the faithful steps forward into the light, and is gone, and the flame roars up the walls.

Algieba.34d4ae9b.text: She smiles, and is herself again, warm and certain. If it frightened her, nothing in her face admits it.

Algieba.367fedcb.text: Before anyone can speak, the air in the hall turns green and gold and smells of marsh water. Someone has come a very long way.

Algieba.37ea9988.text: She looks at him for a long time. Then she smiles, the way people smile at someone who is late, and forgiven.

Algieba.38ead1d3.text: You listen to the mountain and hear nothing at all. No water, no roots. The land is holding its breath, and has been for seventy years.

Algieba.3b090f00.text: Vorga limps east into the canyons. Some of the Host follow him. He doesn't look back to count them.

Algieba.3bbb7613.text: Beneath the pier the river runs shallow over black stone. Something glows in the riverbed, dull red, like a coal at the bottom of a grate.

Algieba.3bc01598.text: We were told to build a hearth. We have built a cage. Gods forgive us if the thing inside ever wakes and wants to go home.

Algieba.3ce89045.text: He drinks, then shuts his eyes and gives his message the way Mother Skarrow made him learn it: slowly, in her own words.

Algieba.3d3fb59a.text: Half the water goes to the party and half to the sand. The elder watches until the last drop sinks into the glass.

Algieba.3fdc53cd.text: At the town's end of the ford bridge, the old Warden stones are slick with steam. Goblin fires burn on the far bank.

Algieba.404bc9b4.text: You can't read him. His face gives you nothing but tiredness, and the patience of a man used to delivering bad news.

Algieba.408f55df.text: His arms carry the clan lines of a hold that froze before you were born. You know the pattern. He doesn't.

Algieba.410d7878.text: She offers a hand, small and hard as a root. When you take it, the children in the tents begin, at last, to whisper.

Algieba.4145cf0a.text: She turns, and the marsh lights turn with her, and a path opens through the reeds where there was none.

Algieba.42bcce4d.text: High on the dark ridge above the camp, a hooded figure stands and watches the fire, and does not come down.

Algieba.43ce6db5.text: Nobody wanted it to come to this. It has anyway.

Algieba.43d63920.text: Oswin Hale: the name at the foot of half the letters in Corvin's archive, the Keeper who swore never to touch the fire. A century gone.

Algieba.43ffd8c5.text: He lifts his grandmother's carved spear, and up on the ridge the Host's drums begin.

Algieba.457af695.text: Pip is singing under her breath: a slow Warden marching song, in words nobody has used for a hundred years.

Algieba.4782b36b.text: The Last Coal, late. The common room is empty, and the hearth burns low on its old shard, red at the edges.

Algieba.4dd39f07.text: Downstream of the bridge, the bank is grey and bare for a mile. Nothing has grown here in a hundred years but one crooked hut.

Algieba.4f242ab1.text: It's over. The living count each other, twice.

Algieba.501b4107.text: Here, on cold ground, they make their stand.

Algieba.50bf6044.text: Out past the firelight, the Vale is cold and very quiet.

Algieba.51f52162.text: And above the caves, a single window in an old watchtower burns with a cold blue light.

Algieba.886d1888.text: Somewhere among the shelves, in a shadow the red light doesn't reach, someone sighs.

Algieba.9042acb0.text: They fall back, and the Vale grows a little colder.

Algieba.91b2e418.text: Steel comes out, and the Vale holds its breath.

Algieba.9761d678.text: It used to be warmer. Nobody in town will say so.

Algieba.9a37642c.text: Your prayer is quiet and old. Her breathing slows to the rhythm of it. Your gift asks nothing of her except to listen.

Algieba.9bf169d3.text: When you kneel beside him, the black armour is empty. The gate of Ember Keep stands open.

Algieba.9c1c2aa9.text: The dead walk by close enough to touch. A pilgrim's lips move without a sound, shaping the same word over and over.

Algieba.9d0e6338.text: You set the ember against the cold one. For one breath the caves glow gold, and every dead thing on the mountain turns its head.

Algieba.9e3232ce.text: The boy repeats it twice to be sure he has it. Then he curls up by the fire, asleep before his tea is cold.

Algieba.9f24b86e.text: The masons wrote in the old dwarven hand, the one you learned from your grandmother's tombstones. You know the word for every kind of stone.

Algieba.a094f05b.text: The wards are careful, elegant work, written to keep the dead out of the caves, not in. Whoever wrote them is protecting something.

Algieba.a27f383b.text: You lift the Sunscar's ember out of the black glass. It is hot as noon, and it leans, very slightly, toward the Keep.

Algieba.a2e6550e.text: Day eleven. The Court sent word. We may leave when we have forgotten why we came. Some of us already have.

Algieba.a69b45f5.text: They are dead. They walk the road they walked in life, and they do not look at you.

Algieba.a73899c6.text: The ledgers blur into orders for stone and lime. Then Pip pulls one free and opens it at a drawing without looking, as if someone had shown her the page.

Algieba.a779ad66.text: The lantern on the pier gutters. When it steadies you are alone, and the ford's ember sits warm in your pack.

Algieba.a7886340.text: The caves of the cold ember are crystal and blue ice, lit from somewhere deep inside. It is the coldest place you have ever stood.

Algieba.a845d540.text: Breath, and blood, and the long walk home.

Algieba.abfab2eb.text: Steam rolls up off the river. When it clears, the far bank is empty.

Algieba.ac41f954.text: The Glimmer Court meets in a hall that is a single willow, grown into vaults and galleries, its branches lit from within.

Algieba.ae24ed85.text: Look closely and you see it. The nearest courtiers are thin as breath, and they lean toward the pool like flowers toward a window.

Algieba.ae874535.text: Next morning a crowd gathers by the chapel steps. A woman in a plain grey coat is speaking, and nobody is leaving.

Algieba.b0874833.text: Nobody has an answer. Somewhere far below, in the dark of the hold, the ice cracks like a door.

Algieba.b2e0e2ee.text: In the Skarrow hills the clan eats well that winter, on Emberwick's grain and the warm valley's harvest.

Algieba.b3320836.text: The crater is a bowl of black glass, too bright to look at. At its edge a white cloth hangs from a spear, and a woman waits beside it.

Algieba.b4ffa202.text: One fewer. It never feels like enough.

Algieba.bdbc247f.text: Its light touches the water, and the water shows you things. A face you had forgotten. A street you used to know. A dog you loved, once.

Algieba.be052fd2.text: You sing the road song Lark taught you. The dead don't turn. But at the second verse a small voice joins in, and it knows a third verse you never learned.

Algieba.be97172f.text: At the Tent of Cool Water, a veiled elder waits at the flap, holding a clay bowl in both hands.

Algieba.becff1c3.text: The last bone Warden falls. Beyond the dais, an inner door bears a seal older than the Fall. It gives at last, onto a vault of shelves.

Algieba.c0229661.text: He fights like a doctor, which is to say he knows exactly where it hurts, and he hates every moment of it.

Algieba.c1d578c5.text: The door slides aside without a sound. Rows of bone Wardens stand at their posts, and on the dais, someone is chanting.

Algieba.c234d0e1.text: She leaves the water and the white cloth where they are, and walks away along the crater's rim without looking back.

Algieba.c31b8691.text: You keep the secret, as the Wardens did. It sits in you like a coal. Every time someone lights a lamp, you know what it is eating.

Algieba.c4139899.text: It is hung with charms of bone and river glass that click in the steam. Someone inside is laughing at you.

Algieba.c4cf8f63.text: Mother Aubrine reads the old scripture once, closes it, and opens her chapel to everyone who is cold. Her faith was in the people, then.

Algieba.c5bcbef9.text: You leave her on the steps. One of the faithful sits down beside her and holds her shoulder, and she lets him.

Algieba.c5d47eba.text: His method is sound. But she has been dead for years. He might give her memories back. He can't give them anywhere to stay.

Algieba.c5f082a9.text: Behind you the Vale goes cold. Frost on the Ashen Ford. The warm fields turn to ordinary mud. The hearth shards dim, one by one.

Algieba.c60fb2de.text: They've won the day. The winter is another matter.

Algieba.c66be6a2.text: Around the flame, the dragon opens one eye. It is the colour of the fire, and it has waited a century to be warm enough to wake.

Algieba.c6c90f31.text: The flame roars up the walls, red as a wound.

Algieba.c8f342c4.text: You know this heat. It is Tobin's forge-fire, the same colour, the same smell, only vast, and failing.

Algieba.cac6e3de.text: No ember-lamp ever burned down here. The Wardens wrote by daylight from a shaft in the roof, and the pages are still white.

Algieba.cb3f75f2.text: The offering slides into the water. The pool hesitates, tastes it, and accepts. A new light blooms, wearing someone else's face.

Algieba.cb61dce4.text: He fights like a man who has practised every morning for a hundred years, because he has. The ash whirls around the blades.

Algieba.cc5f4b43.text: A few spears on the far bank waver. Vorga sees it, and laughs louder to cover it.

Algieba.cc7c551a.text: You chop wood, mend roofs and carry grain. It isn't heroic. It is the work that keeps people alive once the fire is gone.

Algieba.cd98974a.text: On the desk behind him sits Corvin's ember-lamp, unlit for the first time in thirty years.

Algieba.cdf8eac0.text: You lift the Hearthflame from its cage. It is lighter than you feared, and it leans towards the mountains, like a dog that knows the way home.

Algieba.ce25ea28.text: On the oldest shelf lies a Keeper's ledger in a careful, tired hand. It is dated a hundred and eighty years after the Lighting.

Algieba.ce4f5426.text: That winter the fields of the Vale grow warm again. The frost lifts from the Ashen Ford, and Emberwick's granaries are full by midwinter.

Algieba.ce89f197.text: Pip stands in front of the desk. Oswin looks at her for the first time, and his pen stops.

Algieba.cf55a3e5.text: Someone calls a name across the field.

Algieba.d0c2baa8.text: The bridge is gone. Below the stepping stones, Vorga kneels in the shallows, spear snapped, the river pulling at his coat.

Algieba.d1239e6d.text: Ivo kneels in front of her, the way a doctor does, so that his eyes are level with hers.

Algieba.d12d4d8b.text: The hobgoblin hears the party out, sets down his bowl, and answers in a low, careful voice.

Algieba.d18df48d.text: Maren Sorrel sits on the steps before it, her hands blackened, looking at them as if they belonged to someone else.

Algieba.d2f0993d.text: Vorga raises his spear, and up on the ridge the Host's drums begin.

Algieba.d475e7a9.text: The heart of the flame burns low and gold, like a hearth at the end of an evening. The red is going out of it.

Algieba.d48825d5.text: The path into the Skarrow Hills is frozen mud. The camp at the top is smaller than anyone in town imagined.

Algieba.d4bd408d.text: You read the old words aloud. Oswin mouths them with you, word for word, from a memory no fire has ever touched.

Algieba.d5eed908.text: Her finger, crooked as a root, points past you across the steaming water. Someone in a deep hood stands on the far bank.

Algieba.d6f45b81.text: One of them is humming a lullaby you are sure your mother sang. You never told anyone that lullaby.

Algieba.d6ff555a.text: Before the flame stands Maren Sorrel. Behind her a line of the Kindled faithful wait in their best clothes, holding hands.

Algieba.d7a472e8.text: Some days are lost. This is one of them.

Algieba.d7c85c3d.text: At a desk beneath the only window sits a figure in a Keeper's robes, all bone and parchment, writing. He does not look up.

Algieba.d7ffa242.text: You speak for the town that sent you: Bree's hearth, Tobin's forge, the cooling fields. The hall listens as if Emberwick itself were here.

Algieba.d81f1e66.text: The joints are a smith's joints, the kind Tobin Fell taught you. This hall was built like a lock, not a fireplace.

Algieba.d91f17c6.text: Maren's eyes find you in the crowd. She smiles as if you are old friends.

Algieba.da131a08.text: The pilgrim at the front stops, and bows, and walks on. For a moment she looked as if she remembered why.

Algieba.da872c0f.text: It is over quickly. His notes go into your packs. The cold ember, dull and blue in its cave, is yours to carry.

Algieba.daff5262.text: Someone in that hall is waiting. They have been waiting a very long time.

Algieba.dc74fcf8.text: When at last he falls, he goes to one knee first, and sets his sword down carefully, the way a guest sets down a cup.

Algieba.dd70fbe6.text: Courtiers line the galleries. Some are tall and bright. Some are only a voice, or a smell of summer, or a song that stops when you turn.

Algieba.dd8bd366.text: Children watch you from the hide tents. They are too quiet, and their wrists are too thin.

Algieba.decebcee.text: The wind drops, as if it wants to watch.

Algieba.e322d85c.text: You brush the frost from the shrine and speak the old rite. The words come slowly here, as if the cold were listening.

Algieba.e44f9cd8.text: The last page is a single name, written over and over, as if someone was trying very hard not to lose it.

Algieba.e53dd598.text: The first sling-stone cracks against the ice beside you.

Algieba.e58678ec.text: The sand has been dug away from it, and recently. Someone has gone in ahead of you.

Algieba.e5f7defb.text: Outside the inner seal sit the bones of a Warden who came too late to open it. Under one hand lies a last page, written in a hurry.

Algieba.e725b29f.text: The shard in the hearth pops. Bree turns a page, and writes.

Algieba.e75d712f.text: The dragon lies still at last, a hill of cooling coal across the floor. The circle is broken. The faithful who are left weep in the ash.

Algieba.e8ec93fc.text: The light changes. In the doorway stands a woman who was not there a moment ago, pale as birch, dressed in moth wings and dew.

Algieba.e9528ce6.text: Near dusk the road turns, and through the snow you see the dark doors of Greyhold, cut into the mountain.

Algieba.ebc42bc3.text: The ledgers are orders for stone and iron. One is a mason's complaint: the Wardens wanted the flame hall built stronger than the gate.

Algieba.ebe75b6d.text: In the record hall, ledgers climb the walls to the ceiling, each in the careful hand of a mason who wanted to be remembered.

Algieba.ec8f6d0c.text: Coiled around it, scales like banked coals, sleeps a red dragon. Every breath it takes stirs the ash across the floor.

Algieba.ed8a800e.text: You write it in ink, by candle, never by ember-light. Corvin reads every page and copies it twice. It will outlast you both.

Algieba.edb1e14c.text: Nobody answers. She nods, as if someone had.

Algieba.edfc1e02.text: There is no trap in him. Only a man who hasn't slept properly in a very long time, and has stopped expecting anyone to be kind.

Algieba.edff0497.text: You trace the lock in the floor with your hands. Built to hold, never to open. But the masons who built it left their key in the stone.

Algieba.f0608b2b.text: You copy the plans by candle, fingers numb, and never once by ember-light. Some things should not be read by a fire that eats.

Algieba.f0698fa0.text: The flame hall is drawn with walls nine feet thick, and runes of binding over every lintel. A mason does not bind a hearth.

Algieba.f16657bc.text: Somebody laughs. It surprises everyone, and it helps.

Algieba.f40043a1.text: The crowd breaks up slowly. More than a few of them keep looking back the way Maren went.

Algieba.f52f8c99.text: A friend falls, and the others hear it like a bell.

Algieba.f5b46e7a.text: The flame waits. It has waited four hundred years to be asked.

Algieba.f62581b2.text: Ivo Rime comes down from his tower at first light, a doctor's bag over his shoulder and nothing else.

Algieba.f783e2fd.text: By night the river docks belong to the Ash Market. Lanterns float on the water, and nobody uses their real name.

Algieba.f8927bad.text: For the first time in a hundred years the Hearthflame is nearly whole. Now someone has to decide what it is for.

Algieba.f928b794.text: Maren hesitates for a breath. You can see the joints in the walls now, all leaning in. The lock is in the floor, under the dragon.

Algieba.f9391aec.text: Dawn. Mist lies thick on the steaming river, and Dagna's guards wait in the reeds of both banks.

Algieba.fa3e8395.text: Something large shifts in the webs above them. The kobolds see you, drop their picks, and take up their slings.

Algieba.fa641136.text: The offering is clumsy, and every courtier in the galleries sees it. Laughter ripples through the willow, high and cold.

Algieba.fa9ce7a0.text: The last of the clan fall back into the hills, carrying their small ones. None of them look back.

Algieba.fb032e87.text: Mirewood. The road east sinks into black water, and the trees lean close, as if to listen.

Algieba.fc941cd8.text: The caves fall quiet. The kobolds who are left flee up a stair cut into the ice, and at the top of it a door is opening.

Algieba.fd1e9c09.text: A goblin in a chieftain's coat three sizes too big strolls out to the end of the bridge and throws his arms wide.

Algieba.fef3e353.text: Emberwick forgets them, slowly, the way it forgets everything now. The clan does not forget Emberwick.
