Charon.4279cdc8.text: Promise her nothing. Do you understand me? Nothing about the granaries.

Charon.5284baa8.text: A hill clan. Their chief is an old woman they call Mother Skarrow. I've never met her, and I don't need to.

Charon.5448233f.text: Either way, I need that road. I'd like it quick, and I'd like it cheap. I'm not sure I can have both.

Charon.670e9e1c.text: Hunger, I expect. It's been a lean year for everyone, and the hills are always harder than the valley.

Charon.6bb6e964.text: Did she. Of course she did. Tell her the town is handling it. And tell her kindly, would you?

Charon.7574f50d.text: Whatever you think you see, it can wait until the bridge is ours. Please.

Charon.7c780eaf.text: The ford is the only road east. If those goblins hold the bridge past the new moon, Emberwick goes hungry this winter.

Charon.82a7b551.text: People will be calmer if it's you who goes. Calm matters this winter. More than you'd think.

Charon.8c3fe910.text: The Skarrow goblins took the ford bridge nine days ago. Every cart of winter flour comes over it.

Charon.8db36886.text: Mind the frost by the well. That's new. That was never there before.

Charon.8efdc9b2.text: Friends. Thank you for coming. I'd shake every hand, but the light's going, and so is our grain.

Charon.8f6ec162.text: So I locked the grain, let the hills go hungry, and called it prudence. I'm sorry it took goblins to get it out of me.

Charon.9521dde2.text: Thank you. Truly. Emberwick won't forget this.

Charon.955b03a6.text: Ha. My mother would have liked you. Forty crowns from the town chest, and the Last Coal's best rooms till spring.

Charon.ab37b39b.text: A mayor does a great many sums, friend. Most of them come out badly. That's the job.

Charon.ad4cccb1.text: The Marrowbys have been very generous to Emberwick. Very generous. We are all very grateful.

Charon.b63988d0.text: Will you clear them out, or will you talk to their chief?

Charon.d16e8c0c.text: There. That's what I hoped to hear. They still tell the story of you in this square, you know.

Charon.dfd58e43.text: Every winter the warm fields give a little less. I measured it. I told no one, because if I had, half the town would have left.

Charon.e01e3d61.text: If anyone asks, things are well in hand. Are they? No. Don't answer that.

Charon.e05585ab.text: Not now. Please. Whatever it is, not here, not in the square.

Charon.e17dd1f9.text: Trust me, friends. If there were a simpler answer, I'd have found it years ago.

Charon.e6c64b3a.text: There. Forty of them, perhaps. Dagna has eight guards left. And she has you.

Charon.f089eeb7.text: Emberwick has seen hard winters before. We'll see this one through, too.

Charon.ffd896e4.text: The new moon is eleven days off. After that the last carts stop running, and Emberwick starts eating its seed corn.

Charon.fffad5ff.text: It isn't enough, Mother. If we feed the hills, we're short by spring. I've done the sums.

Despina.01c48e59.text: The Court will remember this for as long as there is a Court. You had better hope that is not very long.

Despina.02c2fc61.text: It should. Something has been eating your past, long-lived one. It was not us. Not first.

Despina.06b2c488.text: A bargain is a bargain. I will not lie to make it cheaper, nor to make it dearer.

Despina.07b8986c.text: And nobody even lost a boot. A small miracle.

Despina.0c65007e.text: Our heart lies in the Heartpool, below the roots. You want it. The woman in grey wants it. Everyone wants it.

Despina.0ea4ecdf.text: Tell me something you would hate to forget. Only tell me. I won't take it. Not yet.

Despina.16ecd026.text: We are what it dreamed. Partly. The rest of us is borrowed: things your people set down by their fires and never came back for.

Despina.17849585.text: More of you. The last ones came with knives and shouting. I do hope you will be better company.

Despina.194de6ab.text: Welcome, little flame. Mind where you step. Some of the moss is listening.

Despina.1b090189.text: And the Court parts with nothing for free. Come down to the water. I will name my price there, where you can see what it means.

Despina.217620ad.text: Because you smell of the far side of the mountains. So does the star in our pool. The Court wonders what you are to each other.

Despina.219498f6.text: You have cleared our doorstep. That was a kindness. The Court remembers kindnesses. It also remembers the other thing.

Despina.279121de.text: Choose carefully. Every way is remembered here.

Despina.286e1b69.text: The heart is yours. I cannot break a bargain, not even a bad one, not even a cheat. That is what I am.

Despina.2878a056.text: You have bought the Court's good mood. It is worth more than you know, and it will not last.

Despina.2b612438.text: But the woman in grey will come again, with more knives. When she does, I wonder whether you will wish you had paid.

Despina.34aada15.text: That went better than my last plan.

Despina.4843e567.text: Only one of you need pay. Each of you, decide in your own heart whether you would. I will not ask who. Not yet.

Despina.489dff09.text: But the Court will never forget this. Not in a hundred years. Not in a thousand. Go.

Despina.50d714b9.text: Ah. It knows you. It has never shown anyone that before.

Despina.50fca37f.text: Another question, little flame? Or shall we speak of what you came for?

Despina.531cd7fe.text: How strange you are. I think I like it. Very well. The Court owes you a favour, and the Court always pays.

Despina.53cdace9.text: A pretty attempt. One of the courtiers has stolen your third verse, I'm afraid. You won't miss it until you try to sing it again.

Despina.608efe5c.text: They came with fire and iron to take our heart. So we took a little of theirs. Fair is fair, in Mirewood.

Despina.68a2b90c.text: You keep your memories in such fragile cups. How do you bear it?

Despina.6addb0d0.text: No one ever is. Come anyway.

Despina.7549a12e.text: One day I'll sleep in a real bed. With a pillow. Two pillows.

Despina.78face8a.text: The Court eats it. It becomes a courtier, a lantern, a scent of rain, and it is loved here. It never comes back to you.

Despina.7fcb24d1.text: You are leaving it? After all those reeds?

Despina.7fd30dd0.text: The Court is patient. The Court has nothing but patience.

Despina.8144c6ae.text: A loophole. How mortal. Go on, then. Show the Court something it has never seen.

Despina.842e0f80.text: Your fires are so small out here. I like them. They don't pretend.

Despina.87a0353f.text: I'm fine. Mostly fine. Ask me again in a minute.

Despina.88825a18.text: What else would you know, before you choose?

Despina.8c300f26.text: An elf. How lovely. You have lived so long, and forgotten so much of it. Does it frighten you, the blur where the Keep should be?

Despina.9009ed50.text: Does anyone else remember what we had for breakfast? No? Just me, then. Hopefully.

Despina.996b4dba.text: Names are such sweet things. Yours tastes of smoke, and of something older.

Despina.99c22034.text: Oh, that's nice. Do the other side.

Despina.9c6bf0dc.text: This is the price. Something you would hate to forget. Give it to the pool, and the heart is yours to carry.

Despina.9df23844.text: Without it, I will stop. I find I would like to see how this ends first. That is a very mortal wish. You taught it to me.

Despina.a2b980cd.text: Thank you. I mean it. You gave away something you loved, for strangers. I still do not understand it.

Despina.a6eac2bc.text: There. It is done, and the heart is yours. Lift it, little flame. It is lighter than you think, and heavier.

Despina.a7ed84ce.text: And nobody even lost a memory. Probably.

Despina.ae1b9bc7.text: Forgetting is a door, not a wall. You simply never look back through it.

Despina.aff504cc.text: Then choose. Pay what the Court asks, find a cleverer way, or leave our heart where it lies.

Despina.b18ff760.text: Welcome to the Court. You may sit. You may not eat. You may ask me questions, and I may answer them.

Despina.bba84fa9.text: Forgetting is a door that opens only one way, little flame. Mind which side of it you stand on.

Despina.bbf3ea8a.text: Oh, little flame. I saw the seams in that before you began. But you said the words, and the pool has taken them.

Despina.bde77fd4.text: You are perceptive. Yes. Some of us are made of its light. If it leaves, some of us will stop. Perhaps I will.

Despina.c07eeb4a.text: Not yours. It isn't yours at all. And yet the bargain said a memory, and a memory it was.

Despina.cbf6857c.text: Take the heart. The bargain holds. I cannot break it, even now.

Despina.cc5a81a0.text: You will not even miss it. That is the cruel part, and the merciful one.

Despina.cf0aa4c8.text: Their leader will send more of them. Maren. The name tastes of smoke.

Despina.d108fd32.text: Oh. That was a Warden tune, sung the way they meant it. The galleries are weeping. That is a compliment, here.

Despina.d5b6970d.text: I think I would like to. Go now, before I ask you what it was.

Despina.d754f5bc.text: Little flames. The Court owes you a favour, and the Court pays its debts.

Despina.d7785369.text: Do not trouble your small hearts about the Court. We are not your concern tonight.

Despina.da6dc41d.text: Rude of them to stand there.

Despina.e1b9b641.text: No, no, no. Not you. Not today.

Despina.e79118d5.text: We were the marsh, once. Frogs and reeds and rot. Then a star came down into the water, and the marsh began to dream.

Despina.f303966b.text: Go on, little flames. The Court is watching. We so rarely get a show.

Despina.f8433cf9.text: I am Ysolde. I speak for the Glimmer Court. Come to the willow, little flames, and let us see what you have brought to trade.

Enceladus.0509ac01.text: Then it was for nothing. All of it, for nothing.

Enceladus.1426bc52.text: Yes. I know. A minute, perhaps. I would take a minute.

Enceladus.22a6e522.text: There. Clean. You'll want that bound.

Enceladus.2c18a456.text: Sit. No, there, by the fire. You've been breathing cold air for days. I can hear it in your chests.

Enceladus.2fb7cf65.text: Whoever paid: write down everything you remember around the gap. It helps. It's what I'd tell any patient.

Enceladus.3039477a.text: My name is Ivo Rime. You've come for the cold ember, I expect.

Enceladus.31f6ba1f.text: Hm. You're quicker than you look.

Enceladus.3f6892ea.text: Leave her the brazier. Please. She never liked the cold.

Enceladus.48419d35.text: I can't remember her mother's name. The fire took it. Nell would laugh. She never liked her mother.

Enceladus.53b53e1b.text: Thank you. That was a minute. I said I would take a minute.

Enceladus.59b77082.text: I'm fine. Physicians are the worst patients.

Enceladus.5a7f0979.text: That's heavy. But it isn't a sickness. It's a debt the dead ran up, and it isn't yours to pay alone.

Enceladus.68169e34.text: Ah. Yes. I thought you might. You have honest faces.

Enceladus.6827e27f.text: One of the embers you carry, set against the cold one, for the length of a breath. I'll pay what the fire takes. It's my use, not yours.

Enceladus.789a463a.text: Please don't make me do this. I've so little time left for anything else.

Enceladus.87f4d0a4.text: Go down the mountain. Get warm. Forget you came here.

Enceladus.8e427416.text: Hold still. It's worse if you move.

Enceladus.8e734340.text: I heard her from the tower. Sound carries up here. Let me look at her. No, I'm not asking.

Enceladus.92ff92f0.text: Just under the ribs. I always did know where to cut.

Enceladus.93bac4b3.text: Time of death. No. I don't keep count any more.

Enceladus.9761cf82.text: I'm sorry. You're standing between me and the only thing I have left.

Enceladus.97c11f97.text: Warm it, just a little, with a living ember, and I believe I can give a person back what the fire took from them.

Enceladus.ac911820.text: That will do. They're paid to dig, not to die. Come up, all of you, before your fingers go black.

Enceladus.aeee5b29.text: I'm done with the Kindled. Maren wanted the cold ember lit. It's yours. And whatever else I have, if you ever need a doctor.

Enceladus.babdef8c.text: And then I'll know whether I've spent eleven years on a cure or on a cruelty.

Enceladus.bb71643c.text: I brought her up here because the cold ember raises the dead. It does. She walked, for a while. She didn't know my name.

Enceladus.bd258562.text: Wait. Please. My notes. Don't burn my notes.

Enceladus.c5be32a3.text: Mind the third step. It's ice all the way down. Everything here is.

Enceladus.c925ea14.text: So. Will you let me try? If you say no, I'll fight you for it. I'm sorry. I'm too tired to pretend I wouldn't.

Enceladus.c999ee40.text: They walk, but they don't remember. I wanted to know where the remembering went. I think I know now.

Enceladus.d413d9c7.text: Am I? Well. Doctor's orders, then. I'll see you all down the mountain. After that, keep her warm.

Enceladus.da900dc5.text: Pulse fast. Temperature high, for this cold. Nothing wrong with her that sleep and soup won't mend.

Enceladus.db2579af.text: They don't feel it. I checked. I checked so carefully.

Enceladus.e00f0ace.text: I could try. I won't. Whoever they were, the fire burned them away, and you're the only place they're still kept.

Enceladus.e625767f.text: The memory, though. That isn't going anywhere. Somebody very old put it in very deep.

Enceladus.e6fe8b2b.text: This is Nell, my wife. She died in the hungry years, of a fever I could have treated, if we'd had anything to treat it with.

Enceladus.e8cddb2a.text: Breathe slowly. This will be over soon.

Enceladus.ed816a9d.text: Come in and get warm first. Then we can argue.

Enceladus.f9a75ba9.text: No. I'm sorry. The fire keeps what it burns. The Court doesn't burn, it eats. There's nothing of yours left to put back.

Enceladus.fa2dc34c.text: Fire keeps what it burns. A cold ember still holds every memory it ever took. They're only frozen, like everything else up here.

Erinome.14bcfc9a.text: Retreat is a perfectly valid strategy!

Erinome.274e56ad.text: Exactly as the old treatises describe. With rather more shouting.

Erinome.441a3787.text: I've been counting the stars. There are fewer than in the old charts.

Erinome.62316667.text: Has anyone noticed the gaps in their memories? I'm keeping notes. In ink.

Erinome.6d44882b.text: Has anyone noticed how quiet the old songs go about the Hearthflame? I'm keeping notes.

Erinome.7bd51f67.text: This is less theoretical than I'd like.

Erinome.824c6847.text: Textbook. Literally; I've read the textbook.

Erinome.b2c50804.text: Mind the flanks. Statistically, that's where it goes wrong.

Erinome.ed3b27f4.text: I'll want to examine that later.

Fenrir.0726f773.text: Who's got the stew? I could eat a whole boar, tusks and all.

Fenrir.6394acee.text: Who's got the stew? I could eat a goblin. Not literally.

Fenrir.81c57220.text: Who's buying at the Last Coal?

Fenrir.b7962ce4.text: Just a scratch. A big one.

Gacrux.23c78b29.text: Don't touch the shards. Nothing that glows like that comes free.

Gacrux.728c6215.text: I can't sleep near the fire anymore. Don't ask me why. I don't know why.

Gacrux.c631a814.text: Don't touch the shards. Not if you want to keep your memories.

Gacrux.ce850ce1.text: I forget my mother's face. Did you know that? The fire took it.

Iapetus.03902685.text: Ha! Feel that? That's three winters of hunger!

Iapetus.03911840.text: Go home and tell them! The bridge is Vorga's!

Iapetus.1eacfa68.text: Ha. Ha. Fine. You win the bridge. You don't win the winter.

Iapetus.20568819.text: Everyone's here for me. It's the only bridge! The toll is everything you're carrying, and your boots.

Iapetus.242ece5f.text: Get up! Nobody lies down on my bridge!

Iapetus.24a1b9ae.text: Sorry! Hear that, everyone? They're sorry!

Iapetus.25ebe4e4.text: Go on, finish the set. The Host is watching. Make it a good story for them.

Iapetus.26fab56c.text: Ha. Well. That went about as well as the bridge did.

Iapetus.2ec3aff8.text: I'll remember who did this. I haven't decided yet whether that's a threat.

Iapetus.2f4d8457.text: Run back to your mayor. Tell him to open his granaries, or we come for them.

Iapetus.2f7c0168.text: I buried three cousins while she was being reasonable. Tell her I love her. Tell her she's wrong.

Iapetus.35a1199a.text: She sent you. Of course she did. She always sends someone else to carry things.

Iapetus.378d64fe.text: Take your time. I'm not going anywhere. Mostly because of the leg.

Iapetus.397060be.text: Not like this. Not to them.

Iapetus.3fb795e3.text: That's for the little ones! Every single one!

Iapetus.4116bee5.text: No, keep the boots. I'm feeling generous.

Iapetus.439a5a8b.text: The grain-carriers! Grandmother's new friends! Did she send you all this way to ask me nicely?

Iapetus.45f46213.text: Home to what? A hill full of thank-yous and a third of a sack each? She bargains, and the little ones get thinner.

Iapetus.4d1b81e7.text: Down you go! Down where we've been all along!

Iapetus.4ed060ed.text: Again! Do it again, I dare you to stand up!

Iapetus.505055ec.text: See that, lads? Take a good look. That's what Emberwick looks like up close.

Iapetus.50f4d6f6.text: My lads at the ford said you fought well. The ones who came back said it, anyway.

Iapetus.5c643fce.text: You think blood scares me? I was born hungry!

Iapetus.5de06e90.text: Host! Up, up! The valley's come visiting!

Iapetus.62334472.text: Huh. That's the first time anyone from the valley has said it out loud.

Iapetus.6c77abb7.text: Put me next to her, if you can remember where you left her.

Iapetus.7c5ed39e.text: Lovely speech. Emberwick makes lovely speeches. Then it locks the granary and makes them again next year.

Iapetus.7febf4fb.text: Go on. The Host is watching from the ridge. At least make it look good.

Iapetus.85720d0c.text: Only the towns that lock their granaries. Which, I'll grant you, is all of them.

Iapetus.87837961.text: Changes nothing. But I'll remember you said it.

Iapetus.8b1feef5.text: Lucky! Stay lucky, valley folk. It won't last!

Iapetus.952aceb7.text: Because it was mine. If I can't hold it, nobody walks over it smiling. Not you, not the Kindled, nobody.

Iapetus.986ece2f.text: Look at them! Fat valley folk, all this way just to bleed!

Iapetus.9c4fa205.text: There's the valley talking. Threats, then grain, then threats again. At least mine are honest.

Iapetus.a23e4316.text: Is she eating? Tell me she's eating, at least.

Iapetus.a74705d2.text: Keep it. Sorry doesn't feed anyone. She tried words for forty winters, and look where it got her.

Iapetus.b2fcb32b.text: Home. There's nobody there now to tell me I was wrong. That's the worst part, you know.

Iapetus.b430f812.text: Your side shot first. Then your side came back and finished it. Do you want a medal for remembering?

Iapetus.c00c4dbc.text: I'll remember who let me walk. I haven't decided yet what that means.

Iapetus.c998e359.text: See? Taking works. Asking never fed anybody.

Iapetus.cb5b3b6c.text: Ha! Beaten by the same people twice. Grandmother and grandson both. Somebody should write that down.

Iapetus.d1e2de7c.text: Oh, it's you. I practised a whole speech for this. Give me a moment, it's a good one.

Iapetus.d58c30c8.text: That's all, they say! The road, the grain, the hills, my grandmother. That's all.

Iapetus.e07f1aca.text: You don't get to tell me what she wanted. You don't get to have that too.

Iapetus.e2af221f.text: Home. Tail in the river and a valley mercy on my back. She'll never let me forget it.

Iapetus.eb1e391e.text: Tell her I held it longer than anyone thought I would.

Iapetus.ec52b01f.text: You want my bridge? Come and take it! Come on, I'll wait!

Iapetus.f163a172.text: Every child who starved in the hills is watching you. Make it a good show!

Iapetus.f52de65f.text: She was chief for forty winters. You ended it in an afternoon, on a bridge, over grain.

Iapetus.f6b8c6ac.text: If I let you over, they stop believing me. And then what am I? A hungry boy on a bridge.

Iapetus.fcb8bf7b.text: Ha! Ha ha! Is that all? My grandmother hits harder!

Kore.422f0e3e.text: Hold the line. I've got them.

Kore.d2b5e30f.text: Get some sleep. I'll take first watch.

Kore.e1db609c.text: Hold together. We do this properly.

Laomedeia.0129605a.text: Then listen close. This song is about your side of the mountain, a little. Perhaps it is about you.

Laomedeia.029e8167.text: You ask well. So, a crumb. In the old song the gold is not gold. We sing gold because it rhymes, and the true word is sad.

Laomedeia.051a63e4.text: We never used your fire, so we will remember for you. Somebody has to sing it.

Laomedeia.0bd3bde1.text: Sit. You are guests now, which is worse than enemies. Guests we have to feed.

Laomedeia.0c4bb74a.text: Hm. Well fought. My grandson always said the valley would never share. I should have listened to him.

Laomedeia.10c39c3b.text: His friends will not like a truce. If they bare their teeth on the bridge, do not kill more of them than you must.

Laomedeia.10f68727.text: Seven came down when the snow was still falling, seven came down with their hands full of gold.

Laomedeia.1537e781.text: Here is the bargain, and it is a short one. Your town eats. My clan eats. The bridge goes back to being a bridge.

Laomedeia.159e1253.text: Do not kill him, if you can help it. Beat him if you must. Then send him home to me.

Laomedeia.1646935a.text: Whatever you think of me, feed the little ones. Feed them.

Laomedeia.28789e3a.text: Forty winters I have bled for this clan. Your turn.

Laomedeia.2a51ac9c.text: When the bellies are full, the clan sings. Tonight I sing the old one, because my bones say I should.

Laomedeia.2d77bb31.text: You fed my children. That makes you something. Not family. Not yet. Come back when you are.

Laomedeia.2df5e7c6.text: They will go to him. He will tell them they were brave. They were. Brave is cheap this winter.

Laomedeia.2ecdf337.text: Your Wardens sang that it was given. We never warmed our hands at it, so we never forgot. It was stolen.

Laomedeia.34d15c4e.text: Go down to the river. Tell it Skarrow sent you.

Laomedeia.36254136.text: Half? My children do not eat half. All of it, every week, or go home and fetch your captain.

Laomedeia.370e0656.text: But nobody runs when they carry a fortune. Seven came down, and the seven came running.

Laomedeia.3c34288d.text: You fed my children, valley people. So I give you what I do not give to strangers. Not all of it. The last verse stays with the clan.

Laomedeia.47bc4643.text: Not yet. The little ones have not eaten.

Laomedeia.48c35900.text: My grandson's friends. They would rather die on the stones than eat valley bread. Foolish children.

Laomedeia.4b78081b.text: Come, then. My grandchildren are watching, and they are hungry.

Laomedeia.4fb20358.text: Ha! Somebody's mother taught you properly. You say my name like you have been scolded with it.

Laomedeia.539be9fc.text: You lock your grain and call us thieves. Now you come to finish it.

Laomedeia.5b42a283.text: Forty winters I have held this clan. Do not ask me if I can hold it one more.

Laomedeia.63290733.text: Half now, half at the thaw. You bargain like a hill grandmother. I will take it, and I will watch you.

Laomedeia.6eeeb0bf.text: Hm. I thought you smelled wrong. Not bad. Only far. Like snow from the other side.

Laomedeia.76466178.text: We took the bridge after. Not before. Tell your captain that, if she will hear it.

Laomedeia.7701c3e3.text: That is the next verse. And the next verse is not for strangers.

Laomedeia.77e38814.text: Seven went over the Greywall in the long winters, and seven came back with fire. They came back running.

Laomedeia.793b1ff0.text: But you climbed the hill. So. Sit down again, and agree with me.

Laomedeia.7d34f03e.text: My grandson Vorga holds the bridge you need. He is a fool and a thief, and he is mine.

Laomedeia.823f544c.text: Your captain thinks. Good. Tell her to think about the grain.

Laomedeia.868c4aab.text: I see you, valley people. You came with spears after all. I hoped. I am old enough to know better than hope.

Laomedeia.875961c4.text: Hah. The hill is crooked. Like your mayor.

Laomedeia.879e8008.text: Not coin. Coin does not boil. A share of the grain your mayor keeps behind his locks. Every week, until the thaw.

Laomedeia.89ea0bf0.text: Up, little one. Up. Ah. No.

Laomedeia.917012d5.text: Your song was made by the ones who came home. Ours was made by the ones who watched them come.

Laomedeia.92e6c7da.text: Come, then. Every one of us you kill is one less mouth this winter. Your mayor will be so pleased.

Laomedeia.9688cc6d.text: So. The valley sends swords instead of grain. I expected it.

Laomedeia.a238995d.text: Valley people. Walking. Not running at me with spears. This is new.

Laomedeia.a5f0fd1c.text: Small kindness. Small stomachs. It is not nothing.

Laomedeia.a674fdbb.text: The valley song. Seven went over, seven came home, they brought something heavy. Yes. Pretty.

Laomedeia.a81e4dad.text: Seven went up where the wall meets the sky. No. Not for you. Not for the ones with spears.

Laomedeia.af275c1e.text: Do what you must. But I have buried enough of them this year. Leave me some to scold.

Laomedeia.b6928c58.text: Seven went up where the wall meets the sky, seven with nothing, and hungry, and cold.

Laomedeia.b76444af.text: Then you saw. My little ones were down on the bank, digging roots. Your people shot at them.

Laomedeia.bd7916d9.text: The rest when you are family. Not before. Now eat. You are too thin for valley people.

Laomedeia.bec70ec0.text: I have buried better than you. I will not be buried by you.

Laomedeia.c13a0fee.text: Warm again. Good for the children. But watch. In ten winters you valley folk will forget you owe us grain.

Laomedeia.c1c0ba68.text: Most of them. Some of the young ones belong to my grandson now, in their hearts. Vorga. He left us to take instead of ask.

Laomedeia.d274de5b.text: Go home. Tell them the bridge stays ours until the grain comes.

Laomedeia.d861d152.text: Two-day bread. From the innkeeper, yes? The one who feeds anybody.

Laomedeia.db10f60c.text: Then you know a hill word the valley does not have. It means a debt that both sides pretend is a gift.

Laomedeia.dcccc6e4.text: You lock your grain and call us thieves. Sit. We will talk about who stole what.

Laomedeia.ddf21f82.text: There was a song I meant to teach somebody. Too late now. It goes into the river with me.

Laomedeia.f850cfeb.text: Then it is agreed. Tell your mayor the old mother will give back his bridge. Tell him she is counting the sacks.

Laomedeia.ff119f8b.text: The song says the fire had a home on the far side of the mountains. The seven took it. It was not theirs to take.

Leda.044b9e57.text: A hood. That's all. A hood, and a voice that said, not like this.

Leda.0c8fd9c8.text: And I'm scared that when we get there, I'll know what's behind it.

Leda.0f9fe3c9.text: Can I sleep next to someone? Not because I'm scared. Because it's cold.

Leda.124b0049.text: I don't know that one. I've never heard that one. Why do I keep knowing ones I've never heard?

Leda.16a5dcfe.text: Mister Rime. If you can put memories back into people, can you take them out?

Leda.17b8f77d.text: He's still in here. Oswin. He isn't tired any more. I think I'll keep him. Somebody should.

Leda.186640b5.text: I am Oswin Hale, Warden-Keeper. I have read the oldest books. The fire is not ours, and it is eating us.

Leda.197b4e87.text: Greyhold. The masons kept their books there. How do I know that?

Leda.1e0f981f.text: You came! I told Bree you'd come. The mayor's been asking for you all day, and he's ever so cross.

Leda.1e991ec7.text: She's saying the name of the next shrine. She's been saying it for seventy years. She doesn't know she already got there.

Leda.21712261.text: It hums, in there. It always hummed. I used to think that meant it was happy.

Leda.255a68e2.text: It's so cold now. It was warm here, once. I remember it being warm.

Leda.2622a84e.text: The stars are wrong tonight. No. They're right. I just remember them different.

Leda.2731a214.text: This is where they drew the Keep, before they built it. I know which shelf.

Leda.3eb1ed8d.text: And then someone grabbed his hand. My hand. Someone in a hood, with a cold hand, and they pulled it back.

Leda.3ee4a962.text: And the fire went everywhere. It broke and flew out of the windows like birds. And he was screaming. I was screaming.

Leda.470824cb.text: Halvard. You used to let me win at draughts. No. You used to let him win.

Leda.489a529a.text: I can run that for you! Two coppers. One if you're nice. Three if you're not.

Leda.4b203035.text: There's a door at the top of a long stair, with a crack down the middle. I know exactly where the crack is.

Leda.4dafb332.text: I didn't take it. I was holding it. For you. Here.

Leda.5948a481.text: The fire gave it to me. I think it gave me lots of you. I'm sorry. I didn't ask for it.

Leda.5cbc801c.text: Whatever you pick, I'll still have him in here, and all the others. So you don't have to pick for me.

Leda.6244e4f6.text: Me. I've got ones that aren't mine. Songs, and roads, and a man who's very tired. I don't want to carry him around any more.

Leda.65ca5584.text: We'll leave it. I'll leave a scarf as well. One of them.

Leda.66d19689.text: He's still sitting with her. I know it. Not the fire way. Just the ordinary knowing way.

Leda.6768acc1.text: He was so tired. He's still tired. I can feel it, like a cold in the next room.

Leda.73a24aa2.text: You can stay, if you want. You're less sad than yesterday.

Leda.74591c3b.text: There's a song in my head again. I never learned it. Want to hear?

Leda.7838ac77.text: That one came the same week as the goblins. Never eats. Never sleeps that I've seen. Bree says it's rude to stare.

Leda.7b7df44b.text: I don't know, Bree. I just do.

Leda.84d6c067.text: I am putting it out. Slowly, like a lamp. It is going down, and going quiet, and it is nearly done.

Leda.8e5ca052.text: No face. Just the hood, and the hand. And a voice that said, not like this. Like it was sorry.

Leda.8fa7ec9c.text: I dreamed the river was boiling again. Again's the wrong word, isn't it? I wasn't there.

Leda.9b9a9bb5.text: Can I sit with you? Just till I'm sleepy. I'm not scared. I'm cold.

Leda.9ee57ddd.text: I'm behind the rocks. I'm staying. I'm only looking a little bit.

Leda.a37a0e4b.text: I never used to think anything. I've never been there. Stop looking at me like that.

Leda.a73438bb.text: I didn't see a face. Only a hood. Lots of people have hoods.

Leda.afc3a87a.text: Tell me a story. A true one. I'll know if it isn't.

Leda.b11c13c6.text: I was a man. I was old, and I was in the Keep, in the big hall, and the fire was in front of me, and it was singing.

Leda.b1e9a8b7.text: I know lots of things. I know about the book. And I know Ned's whistle. I can do it.

Leda.c51b0400.text: Down here. Under the third pier, past the eel traps. I don't know how I know that. I've never been under here.

Leda.c8ceb3fd.text: He's looking for his house. He walks up, and it isn't there, so he walks down and tries again.

Leda.d22f8cd8.text: You came. You always come. Don't let them all hear yet. Just you, first.

Leda.da1f2739.text: Bree says I'm not to bother you. I'm not bothering. I'm standing.

Leda.db26b9bb.text: I want Bree to remember Ned. I want the goblin children to eat. I want it to stop eating people. I don't know which one that is.

Leda.dd26df78.text: You were nearly done. It was quiet. And then a hand came over your shoulder, cold, and pulled yours back.

Leda.df10fd65.text: I dreamed of a big stone hall with a fire in the middle. I've never been in a hall.

Leda.e3e3beca.text: They're not dead ones. They're alive ones. That's worse, isn't it?

Leda.e428061e.text: When you go to the Keep, I'm coming. Don't say no. I know the way in. He does, so I do.

Leda.e92089e9.text: Up the grey road, keeper, carry the coal. Mind the cold, for the cold minds you.

Leda.f0e96f71.text: I know a quicker way round the docks. Don't ask how. I just do.

Leda.f103a2dd.text: Bree says the shard in her hearth eats things. Maybe it ate a song, and got lonely, and gave it to me.

Leda.fd8a3c37.text: I don't think grown-ups know either. You just have to pick, and be sorry properly.

Leda.fe2abdb5.text: Bree said I could come if I wore two scarves. I'm wearing three. So that's more than allowed.

Orus.100f98aa.text: Hm. That edge has seen work. Leave it with me.

Orus.3d6bcd97.text: Forge is cold this morning. Colder than yesterday.

Orus.40691a56.text: Shut the door. You're letting the heat out. What's left of it.

Orus.5f9a0165.text: Don't ask where the last shard came from. I didn't.

Orus.c4266628.text: Mm. Good steel remembers the hammer. Better than I do, some days.

Orus.c52a0b96.text: Four Fells at this anvil before me. I'll not be the one lets it go out.

Orus.e61475c4.text: Mm. Bring me the steel. I'll see what's left in the fire.

Pulcherrima.1c30b36e.text: Who's got the stew? I could eat a goblin. Not literally.

Pulcherrima.26bfc3bf.text: Who's buying at the Last Coal?

Pulcherrima.6a11f293.text: Just a scratch. A big one.

Pulcherrima.7182c432.text: Who's got the stew? I could eat a whole boar, tusks and all.

Rasalgethi.02c7aac0.text: So. It ends with tired hands, like everything else.

Rasalgethi.0a16df1d.text: I am Oswin Hale. I remember every year of the Vale's history. You have no idea how heavy that is.

Rasalgethi.1061370b.text: She doesn't remember? No. She wouldn't. She will have lit a great many lamps since then.

Rasalgethi.178603be.text: Seven went over, and seven came home, with a fire on their backs that was never their own. Pay it back, children, or pay what you've known.

Rasalgethi.1a783077.text: Ashby? There was an Ashby who copied for us when I was young. Clever hands. Couldn't spell.

Rasalgethi.20213501.text: Carried, not given. Your church has known for two hundred years. Tell your Mother Aubrine, or don't. That one is yours to choose.

Rasalgethi.23e43572.text: Sit. You gave him back to himself. I owe you the truth, and I have kept it a very long time.

Rasalgethi.3252c0f6.text: Ask what you came to ask. I have had a hundred years to prepare the answers.

Rasalgethi.33a6af41.text: Go home. Remember this. Remember all of it.

Rasalgethi.35b68fc8.text: Every wound has a history. I will remember yours.

Rasalgethi.421c5309.text: Celandine. Nineteen, and frightened, and fast. I saw her run with the chest. I let her go. I thought someone should get out with something.

Rasalgethi.46ff9baf.text: No. Nobody asked. That has always been the trouble with it.

Rasalgethi.57fabfe7.text: Halvard. You have held long enough. Longer than I had any right to ask. I release you.

Rasalgethi.596fcb5d.text: I have been dying for a century. You will have to do better.

Rasalgethi.69918474.text: Sit down. Ah. No one ever sits.

Rasalgethi.71eede65.text: Yes. That is exactly how it was. Child, how do you have that?

Rasalgethi.73baf726.text: I will remember your name. Someone ought to.

Rasalgethi.75ea117b.text: The goblins kept it. Of course they did. They never used the fire, so it never ate their songs. We should have listened to them.

Rasalgethi.7dbe8deb.text: Go, then. I will open the Archive. If the Vale is going to remember, it will want something to read.

Rasalgethi.862de52a.text: The Vale was warm for three hundred years, and paid for every hearth in memory. You know that part. You have read it.

Rasalgethi.897593ed.text: He would. He would say exactly that. I should have released him eighty years ago. I wanted someone to talk to.

Rasalgethi.9796fd80.text: The Kindled. Sorrel is in the flame hall. She is feeding it.

Rasalgethi.9800f0f4.text: Then I will keep it. I have never touched it. Someone in the Vale ought to remember what it costs.

Rasalgethi.9b7e5209.text: Come up. Bring the child. I would like to hear about the hand.

Rasalgethi.9cbc6d1c.text: Bring him, after. Whatever happens. Someone should have all of this who isn't dead.

Rasalgethi.9d1e264b.text: When I was made Keeper I read it too. I swore I would never touch the fire, and I never have. It is why I remember.

Rasalgethi.a0322e5e.text: Hm. Clumsy. I was better at this, once.

Rasalgethi.a67b81aa.text: Sit down. You have killed my only friend and come to ask me questions. I will answer them. That is what I am for.

Rasalgethi.a8f535d8.text: Put it out, and the Vale is cold, and it remembers. I will finish what I began, and go with it. I find I would like that.

Rasalgethi.b4584158.text: A Keeper learned the price two centuries ago, and buried it in the Sunscar. You found his ledger. We went on selling shards anyway.

Rasalgethi.b667fa5d.text: Thank you. Stand back. I know how this goes now. I have had a century to practise it in my head.

Rasalgethi.ba8c16ea.text: You have come a very long way to be wrong.

Rasalgethi.c2b15d0f.text: I made this choice once, for everyone, alone. I was wrong to make it alone. So. This time it is yours.

Rasalgethi.c3914ccd.text: Pain. How very vivid. I had forgotten nothing but that.

Rasalgethi.cd548412.text: Maud is alive? She would have been a child, on the riverbank. Tell her I am sorry she had to see it.

Rasalgethi.dadae810.text: They found a fire on the other side. It was not offered to them. They took it, and they ran home, and they called it a gift.

Rasalgethi.df29d698.text: Not yet. There is still a thing I meant to finish.

Rasalgethi.e25cf88d.text: The last verse. Yes. They stopped singing it on purpose.

Rasalgethi.e268f45b.text: The Keep fell. The Vale burned in five places. Children died in the Sunscar. You did that, so a fire could go home?

Rasalgethi.ea7bc0db.text: On the last night, I tried to end it. I was nearly done. And someone stopped my hand.

Rasalgethi.ea9ea554.text: Gentle. He was always telling me to be gentle. I was never any good at it. He was the gentle one, under all that iron.

Rasalgethi.ed8f401c.text: Four hundred years ago the Vale was cold and starving. Seven people climbed the Greywall looking for anything that would keep their children alive.

Rasalgethi.fd9a2eb6.text: I have kept this hall for a hundred years. I will keep it a little longer.

Sadachbia.21b5fc14.text: The missing years. Forty-one years with no records. Nobody lost them. We burned them. One evening at a time.

Sadachbia.32d55dbd.text: The Wardens must have known. They tended the flame three centuries. Somewhere there are records the fire never touched.

Sadachbia.38f15175.text: Old Maud says I ask the wrong questions. She's usually right, which is infuriating.

Sadachbia.432853b9.text: Partners, then. Two scholars who can't trust their own notes. We'll check each other's. Every page.

Sadachbia.43e2c5b4.text: Here. My notebook. My hand, see? The way I cross my sevens. I'd know it anywhere. Read it. Please.

Sadachbia.4ab8fe56.text: Find them. Please. Before I forget I asked you.

Sadachbia.4f27bcd3.text: If you find anything written down out there, anything at all, bring it to me. Please.

Sadachbia.5a127754.text: Ink. Ink doesn't forget. That's the whole... yes. That's the whole point of ink.

Sadachbia.690be48d.text: Don't touch that pile, it's in order. It doesn't look in order. It is.

Sadachbia.b303661d.text: Mother Aubrine calls history a matter of faith. I call it a matter of paper.

Sadachbia.b42204a1.text: You're back. Good. Thank goodness. I need someone to read something and tell me I'm not, ah. Not...

Sadachbia.c24316e4.text: Thirty years in these records, and forty-one years are simply missing from them. Nobody else seems to mind.

Sadachbia.c6a9da90.text: You too? The same? Then it isn't me going soft, it's real. It's a thing that happens. Oh, that's worse, isn't it.

Sadachbia.c888f978.text: Thirty years reading by ember-lamp, and I can't remember half of what I read. Odd, isn't it?

Sadachbia.cc1591a8.text: Yes! The dwarves write everything down, and even their ledgers have holes. I wrote to Greyhold about it, years ago.

Sadachbia.d6557f44.text: I don't remember writing that. Not a word. It's dated last spring. I've read by that lamp every night for thirty years.

Sadachbia.d9170494.text: Forty-one years, simply missing. Who loses forty-one years? Unless...

Sadachbia.db139977.text: If that's true, then every lamp, every forge, every hearth in the Vale, for three hundred years, we've been...

Sadachbia.e01ff429.text: Ah, you're back! Good. I've found another gap. Well, not found. More... not found.

Sadachbia.fcf46638.text: Old Maud never read by ember-light. She told me so, and I laughed. She's past a hundred, and she remembers everything.

Sadachbia.fe06b700.text: I think I did. I have a copy of the letter. I don't remember the reply.

Sadaltager.018b1c92.text: Ask what you like. I'll answer what I can.

Sadaltager.01e1bcba.text: You've been reading. It shows. People wear that look when they've dug up a debt.

Sadaltager.08c4ba35.text: Exactly as the old treatises describe. With rather more shouting.

Sadaltager.09436a1d.text: I've been counting the stars. There are fewer than in the old charts.

Sadaltager.0bd85432.text: This is less theoretical than I'd like.

Sadaltager.1625a996.text: Because you came to a bridge and chose. Most people let the choosing happen to them. It matters more than you'd think.

Sadaltager.165ca873.text: Mind the flanks. Statistically, that's where it goes wrong.

Sadaltager.1bf837c2.text: I know the road you came by. It's longer than you remember. Don't ask me to walk it with you. Not yet.

Sadaltager.1f309cf2.text: She isn't the only one. There are four more. You'll want to reach them before the woman in grey does.

Sadaltager.201cf514.text: Don't thank me. You may not want to, later.

Sadaltager.20e13d54.text: You noticed the colour. Good. Those shards came a long way, and they don't eat. Sell that to whoever you like. Most won't believe you.

Sadaltager.2255da8e.text: Go and look at your bridge. It's older than your town, and it has seen this before.

Sadaltager.28a727ab.text: Whatever they ask for, think before you say yes. Things given in Mirewood stay given.

Sadaltager.297b4e80.text: People only believe what they dig up themselves. So you had to dig.

Sadaltager.32092c5e.text: Some fires are kept. Some are only borrowed. Few people know the difference.

Sadaltager.3a39654a.text: Yes. I won't pretend it's a warm welcome waiting for you. But it is home.

Sadaltager.3ec2778c.text: Not like this. Yes, I did say that. I'm surprised anyone kept it.

Sadaltager.4262204f.text: Textbook. Literally; I've read the textbook.

Sadaltager.470d5195.text: I want it carried back over the Greywall, to where it was taken from. That's all I have ever wanted. Everything else was waiting.

Sadaltager.48afc5f1.text: Retreat is a perfectly valid strategy!

Sadaltager.4aceabcd.text: Sleep. The road keeps until morning. Most things do.

Sadaltager.4bbae3e1.text: Would you have believed it from a stranger in a hood, in a warm inn, with all the lamps lit?

Sadaltager.59c593e8.text: Someone who has watched a great many rivers. You're asking the right questions. You're just asking the wrong people.

Sadaltager.60f3d594.text: The mountains look close tonight. They never are.

Sadaltager.633a2ce5.text: The nearest lies in Mirewood, where the marsh began to dream. The Court there will want something for it.

Sadaltager.684c4aad.text: Has anyone noticed how quiet the old songs go about the Hearthflame? I'm keeping notes.

Sadaltager.6c002256.text: I'll want to examine that later.

Sadaltager.7075822f.text: I knew you. You stand in a doorway the way your people do. If the fire goes home, so can you.

Sadaltager.71cecafe.text: So it burns again. Someone will notice. I'll be waiting when they do.

Sadaltager.77a1c79c.text: Me. A hundred years ago I stopped your hand. You were about to put it out, and a fire that has gone out can never go home.

Sadaltager.7867142d.text: Has anyone noticed the gaps in their memories? I'm keeping notes. In ink.

Sadaltager.7e34a7a8.text: Someone ought to be waiting at the top of the stair. It's a long climb, carrying a thing like that.

Sadaltager.833d7706.text: We've met before. No? Then we will.

Sadaltager.8be0b877.text: Lovely evening. It won't last. They never do.

Sadaltager.90677fc5.text: I did that. I didn't know it would shatter. I'm not asking you to forgive it. I'm asking what happens next.

Sadaltager.9130e1d2.text: You're asking the right questions. You're only asking them a little early.

Sadaltager.932886ec.text: You found her. Good. She hasn't long, you know. Cracked and chipped, and cold at the heart. Like most things in this valley.

Sadaltager.9d63f457.text: The child sings well. Has anyone asked her where she learned?

Sadaltager.a080a37d.text: Last chance to turn back. No? Good. I would have missed the company.

Sadaltager.a960d3a0.text: Then we can finish arguing afterwards. I'll stand with you for this part, at least.

Sadaltager.b2effea5.text: Because she carries the night I'm most ashamed of, and I wanted to know if it hurt her. It does. I'm sorry for that, too.

Sadaltager.b50f7b87.text: Someone who was here before, and will be here after. That isn't an answer. I know. It's the one I'm allowed to give.

Sadaltager.b5deeddd.text: Or carry it home, over the Greywall, where it was taken from. I'll walk with you. The Vale will be cold, and it will remember too.

Sadaltager.ccb18efd.text: Then it can never go home. I hope you were right. I do hope you were.

Sadaltager.d1a65158.text: Thank you. I have waited a long time to say that to someone.

Sadaltager.d7f741c4.text: She'll keep better near her sisters than in the mud. Leave her here, and the Ash Market will have her in chips by spring.

Sadaltager.ebcb11cb.text: You remember well, Maud. Better than anyone. That was always going to be a problem for somebody.

Sadaltager.f58e8747.text: That is nearly the right question. Not quite. Ask me again one day, on the other side of the wall.

Schedar.17898565.text: The gate is yours. I held it as long as I was able.

Schedar.1b5ca7b8.text: You know that. Nobody knows that. Wait here, if you would be so kind.

Schedar.1d56eca4.text: A message? I may carry a message. That is within my oath. What shall I tell him?

Schedar.1ea19067.text: Well struck. Tell the Keeper I held. Tell him I held it as long as I could.

Schedar.2e1f36a5.text: Come, then. It has been a long while since anyone tried.

Schedar.34e96e62.text: You carry embers. I can feel them from here, like summer. I regret that I cannot let them pass.

Schedar.42501191.text: Ah. There it is. I had nearly forgotten what this felt like.

Schedar.579bab14.text: I love him. I have not forgiven him. Both are still true after a century, which surprises me.

Schedar.57e05ba3.text: You understand, then. I cannot step aside. I can only be relieved.

Schedar.5e89f992.text: Thank you. I had forgotten what it is to want to go somewhere. Be gentle with him. He has been alone a long time.

Schedar.5f3be127.text: Steady. The oath holds, even when I do not.

Schedar.6644cb1b.text: A fair stroke, I hope. I try to keep them clean.

Schedar.69e7aead.text: Child. Where did you learn to say my name like that?

Schedar.6a7af5b8.text: So it reached that far. I am sorry for it. The red came after the Fall. Before, it burned gold, and it was very beautiful, and it was a lie.

Schedar.73a218ee.text: My apologies. That one will not heal kindly.

Schedar.a00c306a.text: I hold this gate for the Keeper. You have my apologies, and my blade.

Schedar.a4fcfe51.text: Well fought. I thank you. I thank you most sincerely.

Schedar.a80d9a35.text: Choose, then. I would rather you turned back. If you will not, I shall try, very politely, to kill you.

Schedar.c718f75b.text: Then you honour me. On guard.

Schedar.cdd08cbe.text: Good evening. I am Halvard, captain of the Warden guard. I hold this gate for the Keeper.

Schedar.d1af1b76.text: Go back down the mountain. Live long. Do not come again.

Schedar.d32bd05c.text: An oath is for keeping. I have kept mine longer than any oath was meant to be kept. That is not the same as it being right.

Schedar.dc1c97b9.text: The hand. He has asked himself whose hand for a hundred years. Wait here, if you would be so kind.

Schedar.e9076bc4.text: Well met. I regret, sincerely, what comes next.

Schedar.eb9fb73c.text: Because the Keeper bade me hold it until he released me, and he has not. He does not leave the archive. He speaks to no one but me.

Sulafat.00fe2089.text: I learned it thirty years ago, when a shard nearly killed me. I woke up remembering winters I never lived.

Sulafat.07f94e5f.text: It doesn't matter whose they were. They were real, and I owe every one of them that world back.

Sulafat.09c96d59.text: I don't want to hurt you. I want you warm. Both can be true today.

Sulafat.0f77ce02.text: You came. I hoped you would. You've carried the embers further than I ever could. Now help me finish it.

Sulafat.10e4d52e.text: No. Please. Don't listen to them. You'll be cold. Your children will be cold.

Sulafat.1450c618.text: Warm fields by spring, if you help me. Full granaries, if the Vale is brave. I can't promise you both by midwinter.

Sulafat.1a820f69.text: A memory for a harvest. I'd make that trade for every child in the Vale. I have made it, over and over.

Sulafat.1b519de0.text: I understand. I'd rather you said no to my face than nodded and lied. The Vale has had enough of that.

Sulafat.23e646e0.text: Ten thousand people will freeze if I don't. I can count. Some nights I wish I couldn't.

Sulafat.2cff742a.text: Then you know it's bearable. You're still here. You're still yourselves, mostly. That's all I'm asking of the Vale.

Sulafat.340a528f.text: Don't tell my people. They need me to be sure.

Sulafat.393e2afa.text: You came. I hoped you would. Sit on this side, the glass is cooler, and the Scarwalkers can see we're keeping the truce.

Sulafat.41a1d68d.text: I stopped asking where they come from. A miracle doesn't owe me an explanation.

Sulafat.424cb940.text: The crater's ember is in the glass below. The Scarwalkers would never let me touch it. You're their guests. Take it to the Keep.

Sulafat.451c0d11.text: Grain for peace. That's beautiful, truly. And when the grain runs out, and the ground goes cold? Kindness won't warm it.

Sulafat.45e0c7b6.text: Rest now. When you wake, it will be warm.

Sulafat.52b79d99.text: I'll remember you kindly. I remember everyone kindly.

Sulafat.54462050.text: One hurt now, ten thousand spared. I've done the sums.

Sulafat.686b1fd8.text: Every one of these people chose this. Eleven lives, and the flame burns again, and ten thousand children are warm this winter.

Sulafat.6a877ccd.text: The truce holds until sundown. After that, I would rather not be your enemy. But I will be, if I must.

Sulafat.6b6d3d53.text: Every fire costs something. The cold costs more. I've buried children who forgot nothing, because they never lived long enough to.

Sulafat.6ed54474.text: My mother's kitchen had blue tiles. Or that was someone else's mother. It doesn't matter. Someone's mother had blue tiles.

Sulafat.707a7698.text: Rook finds them. Some burn a colour I've never seen, and when I use them, they don't take anything at all.

Sulafat.71555ff2.text: If someone over the mountains wants it, let them come and ask. I'll tell them how cold it's been without it.

Sulafat.71b02bf9.text: Kindled, rise. The cold doesn't care if you're tired.

Sulafat.7399eb5e.text: Still standing. Good. There's still time to listen.

Sulafat.7e9b3e9b.text: Or light it. Let them be warm. Let them forget a little. Is a memory worth more than a child who isn't hungry?

Sulafat.809e1605.text: Stolen or given, it kept the Vale alive for three hundred years. I can't hand back three centuries of warm children.

Sulafat.84a29a01.text: Bring the embers to Ember Keep, and stand beside me when we light it. Not for me. For them.

Sulafat.85b97cd4.text: I had a plan. I was the only one with a plan.

Sulafat.89395da9.text: Maren. That's a good name. I think I would have liked her. Did she do much harm?

Sulafat.91e47426.text: Honestly? Some nights I can't find myself in there. Hundreds of lives, and I have to go looking for mine.

Sulafat.9422c710.text: Then who keeps them warm? Tell me that. Who?

Sulafat.965686b3.text: You've felt the cold. Stand with me, or stand aside.

Sulafat.97f3d2fa.text: It doesn't have to be this way. The Hearthflame can burn again. It wants to. It only needs us to be brave enough to feed it.

Sulafat.9fbc0f8b.text: I'm sorry. I'll carry that one too.

Sulafat.a2275dbe.text: Ask me anything. I'd rather you heard it from me than from a pulpit.

Sulafat.a407c9aa.text: You found it, didn't you? Under the docks. I can see it on you. Tell me, what did the ford cost you?

Sulafat.a594c60c.text: I feed it the willing, and I won't pretend that's clean. I hold their hands. I keep their names, for as long as I can.

Sulafat.a81e33f9.text: Your warmth goes into the flame now. It won't be wasted.

Sulafat.a91b2478.text: Then I'll see you at the Keep. I hope we're standing on the same side of the flame.

Sulafat.a95264b6.text: I know. He wrote to me. He said he'd had his minute, and it was enough. I'm glad for him, truly. Not everyone gets a minute.

Sulafat.aaa19d46.text: I'm sorry. He was angry for all the right reasons, and nobody ever fed him long enough to find out what else he was.

Sulafat.b292770f.text: I know. You left him sitting with a dead woman in the cold. I'm not the only one here who weighs lives, am I?

Sulafat.b493921a.text: That's all I ask. Think. Then look at the fields this winter, and think again.

Sulafat.b82db7b8.text: You've been in the crypt, so now you know what the fire takes. I'm sorry. It's a hard thing to carry out into the sun.

Sulafat.c472266b.text: Not yet. They're all counting on me.

Sulafat.cc36f386.text: You've felt how cold it's getting. The fields. The forges. Your own hearths, a little lower every year.

Sulafat.ce27c406.text: Mother Aubrine. You fed half this town last winter, and you'll bury the other half this one. I'm offering more than prayers.

Sulafat.d9cc3a05.text: Good. I offered him bread for that bridge, and he threw it in the canyon. I liked him for it.

Sulafat.e46ff3a3.text: So did I, once. It frightened me how easy it was. It should frighten you a little, too.

Sulafat.e50224f9.text: I remember the Hearth Age. Warm winters. My mother keeping bees on the south wall, singing to them.

Sulafat.eb424ada.text: I know. So I'll have to go back for it, and Ysolde will make me pay. I wish it had been you.

Sulafat.edc72231.text: Every winter we argue, more children freeze. Let's not argue.

Sulafat.ee1914e1.text: Then I'm sorry. I'll remember you. I remember everyone.

Sulafat.f0a8cc85.text: A cage keeps things in. That's all I want. Warmth, kept in, for us.

Sulafat.f1bea43d.text: Come and find me when you're ready to save the Vale, and not only this town. I'll be wherever the embers are.

Sulafat.f714da20.text: Then you understand already. Sometimes one life buys a winter for a thousand. That isn't cruelty. It's arithmetic.

Sulafat.fa963bba.text: No. That wasn't my mother. That was someone's. I'm sorry, it happens. There are so many of them in here.

Sulafat.fcf5927e.text: I've felt worse. I remember being worse.

Sulafat.ffe703c8.text: I can't find my name. I know hundreds of names. Which one was mine?

Umbriel.0f6a78f0.text: Here's something for free, since I'm feeling generous. I sell more shards than this ember has to give.

Umbriel.1e0fe471.text: Mind the docks after dark. Not everyone down here is as friendly as me.

Umbriel.44e9d184.text: Fine. Put it on my tab.

Umbriel.457031ab.text: She was dying long before I came. I sell the pieces before they're worth nothing. That's not murder. That's timing.

Umbriel.4df7e8a4.text: There you are. Wondered when the river would bring you back. You still owe me, you know.

Umbriel.6c66359e.text: You didn't see me. That one's free.

Umbriel.7705fd5a.text: Everybody wants the same thing in the end. I just get there first.

Umbriel.805db8d9.text: Last offer. Walk away and I forget your faces.

Umbriel.81685659.text: Shards, word, a boat at midnight. All for sale. Which do you need?

Umbriel.a572e698.text: Rook. I run the Ash Market. You've bought from me, or your grandmother did. Everyone has.

Umbriel.b53f5a4f.text: Funny thing. I'm selling more shards than the Vale ought to have. Don't spread that about.

Umbriel.c2f15317.text: Yes, we chip her. A shard here, a shard there, and somebody's hearth stays warm. Shame to let it go to waste in the mud.

Umbriel.c81bb511.text: Somebody else supplies the difference. I don't know who. I'd like to, before they decide they don't need me.

Umbriel.caf09b79.text: All right. All right. Let's talk terms.

Umbriel.caf2184d.text: Prices went up. Everything's colder, and cold costs.

Umbriel.cb99b723.text: Here's how you pay. I'm selling the Kindled more shards than exist in the Vale. Find who's supplying the rest, and we're square.

Umbriel.e29071c8.text: Careful. You're standing on my livelihood.

Vindemiatrix.0643e496.text: I buried two this week, old ones, cold in their beds. Pray it stays only the old.

Vindemiatrix.152fd558.text: Come in out of the wind. There's soup at the back, and nobody counts the bowls.

Vindemiatrix.3e5cda96.text: We were all warming our hands at a fire you knew was dying. Gods forgive you, Halden. I'm not sure I can, yet.

Vindemiatrix.4410ca9d.text: Maren Sorrel. I put you out of my chapel once. Don't make me do it to the whole square.

Vindemiatrix.4cc57b2f.text: Mind how you speak in the square. Fear spreads faster than fever.

Vindemiatrix.68c86225.text: But you came home when I wrote to you. Here. The archive key. Bring it back, and bring me what you find.

Vindemiatrix.831a18f3.text: You always did find the sharp end of a sermon. Very well. The chapel opens its stores first, and in public.

Vindemiatrix.8da99f5f.text: The chapel can spare its tithe barley. It isn't much. But no one sent to my door has ever been turned away.

Vindemiatrix.8e16f7e4.text: Pray if you like. If you'd rather not, sit anyway. The chapel doesn't mind.

Vindemiatrix.a29eef99.text: Doubt is a draught under the door. Shut it, and keep the hearth.

Vindemiatrix.a649f7ee.text: Corvin says the records have holes in them. Corvin says a great many things.

Vindemiatrix.c2513b6a.text: Then we shall see who in this room is willing to be seen giving less than the church.

Vindemiatrix.cbdc6077.text: Be careful of her. The worst of it is that she believes every word.

Vindemiatrix.ecdca431.text: The flame was given to us. We will be worthy of it, cold or warm.

Vindemiatrix.f634b447.text: The cellar texts? No one has read those in my lifetime. They're very old, and very dull, I'm told.

Zephyr.02311538.text: I'll keep the stew warm. For whoever comes back across.

Zephyr.04bf9fbe.text: She sent a little one down for bread in the spring. Asked at the granary gate, polite as you like.

Zephyr.11f3a189.text: Stew's hot, bread's yesterday's. Don't complain, my love, nobody else is feeding you.

Zephyr.163bb66a.text: My best rooms. He means my only rooms. Still. Done.

Zephyr.1e062eb2.text: And do what? Half this street sleeps by my hearth when the snow comes. I'll not freeze them to keep a man I've already lost.

Zephyr.1e4e2be0.text: So I write him down. Everything I've still got. Look. Ned whistled through his teeth when he was nervous. Ned hated eels.

Zephyr.2b0fe173.text: Heard a thing at the bar you'll want to hear. Eat first.

Zephyr.2bc25003.text: Sit. Eat. Then you can tell me how bad it is. Mirewood, of all places. Were the stories true?

Zephyr.2eb01dac.text: And the ones who don't break, Dagna? The ones with nowhere left to run to?

Zephyr.3ab30cff.text: Gave it away? On purpose? And now you don't know what it was?

Zephyr.3adb637b.text: His face went first. Then his voice. I'd sit by this hearth trying to remember, and every night there was less of him.

Zephyr.4e60228c.text: He sang terribly. Properly terribly. Write that down. Write it twice.

Zephyr.50fe9826.text: It's the fire. I know it is. The nights I sit closest are the nights I lose most. Gran's shard. Gran's lovely Warden shard.

Zephyr.50ffb190.text: Pip! Where's that girl got to? Never mind. She'll turn up when she's hungry.

Zephyr.57211e76.text: Oh, no you don't. Up you get, my love. Up!

Zephyr.5b927ecc.text: Sit. Eat. It's going to be a long winter, and we'll need everyone's hands for it.

Zephyr.5d6a5149.text: Not a word to the town. They've enough to be frightened of this winter. Promise me.

Zephyr.5f082afc.text: I've something to show you. Not Pip. She's asleep, and she's enough on her plate.

Zephyr.6390da08.text: Come in closer. The fire doesn't bite, and neither do I. Much.

Zephyr.63a7d3bb.text: No. I'll keep it lit, and I'll keep writing. That's the bargain. I made it without knowing, but it's mine now.

Zephyr.6c380dd7.text: Boots off the benches. I'll not tell you twice. Well, I will, but I'll not like it.

Zephyr.76af17da.text: I'm all right. I'm all right. Keep going.

Zephyr.76ddf0fc.text: Pip Ashdown, you're meant to be asleep. You never met him, love. How would you know his whistle?

Zephyr.7b4225c3.text: Halden lied so folk wouldn't leave. I'm only keeping my own grief to myself. That's not the same. Is it?

Zephyr.8921dbc8.text: Ned whistled through his teeth when he was nervous. Did I ever tell you? I don't need the book for that any more. I remember.

Zephyr.8fe64c92.text: Bread. Two days old, but it's honest. Take it up the hill. Children first, mind.

Zephyr.95fb71ea.text: I'm still writing Ned down, every night. Some nights I read it back and I don't know who it's about.

Zephyr.9631eff2.text: Go on, then. Go and give it back. I'll burn wood. We managed before the fire, and we'll manage after it.

Zephyr.979ffcb8.text: Sit. Eat. Warmest winter of my life, and I've the soup to prove it.

Zephyr.99639f3f.text: And here's mine. That's a whole people up there, and they're hungry for the same reason we are, only worse.

Zephyr.9d5e4532.text: Pip, let them breathe. You lot, there's stew when he's done with you. Don't let him talk it cold.

Zephyr.a60b216f.text: Leaner for them. We had the warm fields. They had snow on their fires by the Harvest Month.

Zephyr.aeacefe3.text: Brought you a pie. Don't look at me like that, you're thin as rakes, the lot of you.

Zephyr.c0e17f8d.text: Ned sang flat. He burned the bread. He laughed like a goose. I remember. I remember all of it.

Zephyr.c3f9e45f.text: Right then. I've thrown worse than you out of my inn.

Zephyr.c9c70f13.text: Oh, my love. Come here. I know what that's like, I think. Better than I'd want to.

Zephyr.cd4b734f.text: Sit. Eat. Then you can tell me how bad it is.

Zephyr.cf40c03a.text: Good. Now everyone's coming back for supper, and no arguments.

Zephyr.d96c5951.text: Folk will say you came home empty-handed. Let them. Sometimes that's the hard thing, and the right one.

Zephyr.db6d9b1f.text: My husband. Ned. He drowned at the ford, eleven years back. And I've been losing him. Not the grief. Him.

Zephyr.dea03243.text: Would you? Ask me things, then. Anything. If I still know it, it goes in the book.

Zephyr.e6d409fe.text: I don't remember writing that one. About the eels. It's my hand. I must have known it, once.

Zephyr.e9cb51e7.text: Left it? Good. Whatever it was, it wasn't yours, and it sounds like they need it more than we do.

Zephyr.ef329ccf.text: Bad dreams and too much cheese, that's all. In you come, Pip. Bed.

Zephyr.f2a2cb51.text: Thank you, my love. Your supper is on the house.

Zephyr.f3f2a59d.text: You cheated the fey. Course you did. My gran would've hung a horseshoe on you and bolted the door.

Zephyr.f49fbc2d.text: Kill their mother and you've bought a bridge for one winter. Her grandsons will remember it for fifty.

Zephyr.faecf1ce.text: Whose memory was it, then? Somebody's. Somebody had it once, and wanted it.

Zubenelgenubi.0eba04cc.text: I'm fine. Mostly fine. Ask me again in a minute.

Zubenelgenubi.1e88eaac.text: Oh, that's nice. Do the other side.

Zubenelgenubi.435389f8.text: And nobody even lost a boot. A small miracle.

Zubenelgenubi.713bcca3.text: That went better than my last plan.

Zubenelgenubi.8b915fee.text: No, no, no. Not you. Not today.

Zubenelgenubi.a195f95b.text: One day I'll sleep in a real bed. With a pillow. Two pillows.

Zubenelgenubi.b8d4ea15.text: Does anyone else remember what we had for breakfast? No? Just me, then. Hopefully.

Zubenelgenubi.d91f4576.text: And nobody even lost a memory. Probably.

Zubenelgenubi.f32e6ba4.text: Rude of them to stand there.
